questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That is was within Europe due to Erasmus

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only reason I don't give it a 10/10 is because I was not able to get any of the courses I initially wanted

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In beginning it felt like the information was coming from mulitple sources, so it felt more confusing that it may actually was

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A great international mobility office was ready to help with anything!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We unfortunately didn't get any introduction to the university and teaching itself ...

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Same as in Copenhagen - it is expensive and really difficult to navigate in the system of when am I being fooled and when is it legit. Best advice is to trust the prices.. It should be more or less the same as in Copenhagen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Milano have so much to offer so do not be scared to live off campus!! They have great transportation and infrastructure (at least during the day) 
But if possible, I would recommend to stay inside the "walls" - meaning inside the circle surrounding Milano when you look at a map. Every area is different, but has their own thing to offer, so don't worry too much about the specific area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a mobility office, where you can find every information - they are great at communicating the information

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online and office hours - really easy to reach by mail as well

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: A lot of the classes I initially wanted, wasn't avaliable - so ended up choosing what made most sense (in regards to work load and schema)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The italian students on their master, are to choose a couple of classes themselves, therefore the first one-two weeks is considered a "try-it-out-period" and you can shuffle around different classes, to find the ones that suits you. So don't stress too much about it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took master level courses (and I am bachelor level in CPH) and I would say it was easy enough to follow along. 
I had 4 courses, two 6 ects and 9 ects. Workload wise it was perfect. But I would say the expectations are very different from course to course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The style of teaching is the same - but the exam forms are very different. 
It was usually a written test (yes written by hand) with 3-4 open questions and duration 1-1.5 hour. I also had a multiple-choice-exam - really weird when it is social science - but I would say It was easy enough if you had followed along and did some studying beforehand.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Social Dynamics 9 ECTS 
Globalization, Human Rights and Social Justice 6 ECTS 
Value Change and Global Societies 6 ECTS 
Journalism, Media and Politics 9 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Value Change and Global Societies - really great teacher 
Globalization, Human Rights and Social Justice - really interesting topics

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: must admit i didn't partipate in any...

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: anything from volley ball to trips to Rome - there was a really great erasmus exchange program every month

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I haven't participated in any - but I would say going to the first party - seemed like a lot of relationsship were made there

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Please spend time seeing different parts of the city, it is so much more than city center!! 

Otherwise take a trip to Bologna, Lake Como and Parma!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I loved it. So very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out at night!! Italians are so friendly when they have a drink in hand

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I was surprised that not all young people could speak English..

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openminded approach to exchange students - really often got asked where I was from and if I liked it in Italy... Annnnd quickly follow-up by recommendations and picture and stories from their home town

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
There will not be happening exiciting things all the time .. a lot of the time you will have a normal everyday-life so be prepared to take initiative to make friends and make plans if you want to do something. 

It is easier to live up to the criterias than in Copenhagen, but you will still need to participate and do your stuff 

Do not underestimate Milanooooo <333

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I participated the autumm trimester (september to december)

The courses began september 15th and it was possible to take all the exams during december. 

it is possible to take all exams on three different dates - in our case, during december, january and in march

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting familiar with a city

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: all the empty hours where you do not have plans

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
